title: enterprise-invoice-failover-and-collection-escalation-playbook
author: Michael Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the standard operating procedure for handling invoice delivery failures, payment collection retries, and staged escalation for overdue accounts across our hosted, dedicated, and private product lines. It covers automated retry logic, communication templates, accounting impacts (deferred revenue / revenue holds), thresholds for collections and legal handoff, ownership, monitoring, and postmortem steps.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all invoices generated by Redwood Inference billing systems (hosted API usage, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private deployments add-ons).
- Includes all currencies and regions where Redwood operates (North America, Europe, APAC).
- Excludes one-off refunds and chargebacks handled under the Refunds SOP (see Related pages).

Definitions:
- Invoice Failure: any delivered invoice that is flagged as undeliverable (email bounce) or that fails payment collection (card decline, ACH return, bank rejection).
- Dunning: sequence of communications sent to a customer to request payment.
- Revenue Hold: temporary flag in the accounting system preventing revenue recognition for a given invoice.

Ownership and stakeholders:
- Billing Operations (BillingOps): primary owner of invoice delivery, retry orchestration, and dunning cadence. Contacts: billing-ops@redwood.ai, primary owner: Priya Kapoor.
- Collections: responsible for outreach beyond automated dunning (phone calls, account managers). Escalation owner: Luis Fernandez.
- Legal & Commercial Contracting: engaged for accounts >$250k ARR or complex disputes. Contact: legal@redwood.ai.
- Revenue Accounting: advises on revrec treatment and GL posting. Contact: revrec@redwood.ai.
- Customer Success & Account Management: coordinate customer communication for strategic accounts.

SLOs and targets:
- Invoice generation and initial delivery: 99.9% within 60 seconds of batch run.
- Payment event processing latency: <= 30s for API-based payments.
- Automated retry initiation for transient failures: 100% started within 2 hours of failure detection.
- Escalation to Collections for past-due >30 days: 100% of qualifying accounts within 24 hours of threshold.

Failure categories and response matrix:
| Failure type | Immediate action | Escalation threshold | Accounting impact |
| Email bounce (delivery failure) | Mark invoice undeliverable; attempt alternative email on record; notify Account Manager | 7 days, if undeliverable -> manual outreach by CS | No immediate revrec impact |
| Card decline (soft) | Trigger automated retry schedule (0h, 6h, 24h, 72h) and send dunning email | If still failing after 4 retries (~7 days) -> Collections | Mark invoice as at-risk; hold revenue recognition for usage invoices >30 days unpaid |
| ACH return / bank reject (hard) | Flag as hard failure; send instructions + invoice link | If unpaid after 5 business days -> Collections; consider invocation of contract collection clauses | Place invoice on revenue hold immediately if material |
| Invoice disputes (billing disagreement) | Open a dispute ticket in BillingOps queue; notify Legal if contract terms cited | If unresolved >30 days and >$50k -> Legal review | Follow dispute accounting: reserve or offset per RevRec guidance |

Automated retry logic (BillingOps runbook):
1) Detect failure: listen for payment.failed and invoice.delivery.failed events from payment gateway webhook.
2) Classify failure: soft vs hard (use provider error_codes mapping).
3) Soft failures: schedule retries: T0 (immediate), T+6h, T+24h, T+72h. After each retry, send templated dunning message.
4) Hard failures: do not retry automatically; switch to manual collection workflow and present next steps in UI.
5) Retry orchestration pseudocode (example):
```
# invoices-cli pseudo
invoices-cli watch --event payment.failed --filter "region=eu|na|apac" | while read ev; do
  if is_soft_error(ev.code); then
    schedule_retry(ev.invoice_id, [0h,6h,24h,72h])
  else
    mark_hard_failure(ev.invoice_id)
    create_task("collections", ev.invoice_id, ev.reason)
  fi
done
```

Dunning cadence and templates (examples):
- Day 0 (payment attempt failed): Short advisory email + link to retry payment.
- Day 2 (after 2 retries): Reminder + impact note (service interruption potential).
- Day 7: Escalation email from Collections with POC phone number.
- Day 30: Final notice — next step includes service suspension and legal collections.

Sample dunning email (Day 2):
Subject: Action required: Payment for Redwood invoice #{{invoice_id}}
Body:
Hello {{billing_contact.name}},

We attempted to process payment for invoice {{invoice_id}} ({{amount}} {{currency}}) on {{due_date}} but were unable to complete the transaction. Please update your payment method at {{payment_link}} or contact billing-ops@redwood.ai to resolve.

If we do not receive payment within 7 days the account may be moved to collections.

Best,
Redwood Billing Team

Accounting and revenue recognition guidance:
- Usage-based invoices: revenue is deferred until payment is collected for customer accounts flagged as high-risk (per the decision matrix below). For low-risk accounts we may recognize on invoice issuance per ASC 606 policies documented in RevRec playbook.
- Commitment/contract invoices (reserved Dedicated capacity): if contractually invoiced in advance, recognize revenue over the contractual service period unless a material collection concern exists — then mark as deferred and re-evaluate quarterly.
- Dispute accounting: create a contra-revenue or reserve entry for the disputed amount, with justification and ticket ID recorded.

Decision matrix for revenue hold (table):
| Criteria | Action |
| Overdue >30 days AND invoice amount > $50,000 | Place on revenue hold; escalate to Collections + RevRec review |
| Overdue >60 days OR evidence of insolvency | Place on revenue hold; legal review and possible impairment reserve |
| Customer under active contract termination notice | Evaluate contractual terms; consult Legal before recognition |

Cross-border and tax considerations:
- For cross-border invoices, BillingOps must validate VAT/GST registration numbers before reattempting auto-collect for EU/APAC customers.
- Currency conversion policy: when retries occur in a different settlement date, apply the FX policy in the Accounting FX manual; record realized gains/losses to GL 5420.

Manual collections workflow (steps):
1) Collections creates outreach log entry and attempts 3 phone calls across business days.
2) If no contact after 10 business days, Collections issues an escalation email copied to Account Management and Legal.
3) For strategic accounts (> $250k ARR), Collections schedules an account review call with Customer Success and the Account Executive.
4) If account still unpaid after 45 days, Collections issues a formal demand letter. Template stored in /legal/collections-templates (internal repository).

Legal handoff checklist (when >60 days or >$250k):
- Attach full payment history, retry logs, all communications, signed contract, PO (if provided), and any support tickets referencing the invoice.
- Confirm internal approvals: Head of Revenue, Head of Legal, and Finance Controller sign-off.
- If litigation or collection agency engaged, freeze further automated retries and flag account in the CRM as "legal_hold".

Operational monitoring and dashboards:
- Key metrics to monitor: failed payment rate by gateway, retry success rate, days sales outstanding (DSO), number of accounts in collections, top 20 overdue accounts.
- Daily alert thresholds: >1% global failed payment rate triggers Paging to BillingOps on-call.
- Weekly report: Aging bucket summary (0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+) and top 10 revenue at risk.

Audit, logging, and evidence retention:
- All retry attempts, webhook events, and outbound communications must be retained for 7 years in the billing audit log.
- Attachments for legal handoff must be stored in the restricted evidence bucket with access logging enabled.

Post-incident review and learning:
1) After any major collection incident (> $100k realized as bad debt or an outage caused by billing failures) run a retrospective within 7 business days.
2) Deliverables: incident timeline, root cause, remediation plan, owner assignments, and follow-up verification dates.

Appendices:
A. CLI snippets for ad-hoc investigation:
- List overdue invoices older than 30 days:
```
billing-db query "SELECT invoice_id, customer_id, amount, due_date FROM invoices WHERE status='overdue' AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'"
```
- Export retry log for invoice 12345:
```
billing-ops export-retry-log --invoice 12345 --format csv > retry-log-12345.csv
```
B. Escalation contact list (roles only):
- BillingOps on-call: billing-ops-oncall@redwood.ai
- Collections lead: luis.fernandez@redwood.ai
